serverInfo.name: rmcp
serverInfo.instructions: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.
serverInfo.clientInfoNote: The package's own identity was accepted by the runtime (inventory, browser inventory, elicitation path all worked), so Codex's `codex-mcp-client` identity is not imitated.

toolRegistration.description: server `tools/list` description verbatim (changes with CUA_REPL_ENABLED_SURFACES; computer-only contains `Browser APIs are disabled.`)
toolRegistration.parameters: server inputSchema verbatim (type/properties defaulted when missing)
toolRegistration.annotations: boolean hints verbatim (js, js_reset: readOnlyHint true, destructiveHint false, openWorldHint false)

modules.src/connection.ts: composeEnvironment(plan, state, hostEnv), enabledSurfaces(state), openConnection({plan, state, log, clientInfo?, elicitationHandler?}) → BridgeConnection {client, pid, serverInfo, protocolVersion, instructions, tools, environment, startedAt, setElicitationHandler(handler), isClosed(), onClose(listener), close()}; LoggingTransport wraps StdioTransport so every JSON-RPC message is logged redacted; PROTOCOL_VERSION, DEFAULT_CLIENT_INFO.
modules.src/tools.ts: registerBridgeTools(pi, connection | undefined, deps, previousNames) → registered names; buildCallMeta({callId, sessionId, turnId, turnStartedAtUnixMs, model}); convertCallToolResult(result, {tool, limitBytes, durationMs}); truncateMiddle; constants SERVER_NAME, EXPOSED_TOOLS, NAMESPACE_NAME, TOOL_NAMES, BYTES_PER_TOKEN. Dependencies: getConnection, ensureTurn, log, describeServer, onCancelled?.
modules.src/turn.ts: TurnTracker {begin(), ensure(), currentTurn, recordOutcome(outcome), settle() → SettledTurn}; hookEventNameFor(outcome); notifyTurnEnded(connection, sessionId, settledTurn, log) with a 120 s request timeout.
modules.src/log.ts: BridgeLog(path).write(kind, payload) → `<iso> <kind> <json>` lines, redaction of keys matching /token|key|secret|account|password|cookie|authorization/i, 64 KiB per line, rotation to `.1` past 5 MiB; redactSecrets().
modules.src/index.ts: session_start → load settings, start server when a flag is on (closing any previous connection first), register tools; agent_start → new turn id; agent_end → detects aborted runs from the last assistant message; agent_before_settle → outcome; agent_settled → turn_ended (not awaited); session_shutdown → close; command updateState → save, restart, re-register; describeServer() for status output.

elicitationHook.how: openConnection registers one `elicitation/create` request handler on the McpClient; `BridgeConnection.setElicitationHandler(handler)` swaps the implementation at any time, and `openConnection({ elicitationHandler })` installs it from the start. 04-confirmations should install its handler right after `openConnection` resolves in index.ts (`startServer`), before tools are registered.
elicitationHook.handlerSignature: (params: ElicitationParams {message?, requestedSchema?, _meta?}, context: {signal}) => ElicitationResult {action: accept|decline|cancel, content?, _meta?} | Promise
elicitationHook.placeholder: logs `elicitation-unhandled {message, meta}` and answers `{action: "cancel"}` — so app access fails with `Computer Use was not approved to use <App>` until 04 lands
elicitationHook.observedRequestShape: see 02-feasibility.json elicitation.requests: message `Allow Computer Use to use "<App>"?`, empty object schema, _meta {callId (echoes the tools/call callId), codex_approval_kind mcp_tool_call, connector_id computer-use, connector_name, persist [session, always], progressToken, riskLevel, tool_name get_app_state, tool_params {app: bundle id}, tool_params_display, x-codex-turn-metadata (echoed)}

resultConversion.content: toLlmContent(result): text and image blocks; text joined and middle-truncated past outputTokenLimit × 4 bytes (100000 bytes for the .mcp.json value 25000) with Codex-style header `Warning: truncated output (original token count: N)` and `[Full output: <tmpdir>/pi-codex-computer-use-<hex>.txt (read it with offset/limit)]`; full text saved with mode 0600
resultConversion.images: pass through as ImageContent (verified: nodeRepl.emitImage data URL → image block → model reported receiving an image)
resultConversion.isError: MCP isError → pi isError result; empty error text gets `MCP tool cua_repl/<tool> returned an error`
resultConversion.replOutputBehavior: The REPL does not echo bare expression values (`"a".repeat(100)`, `1 + 1`, objects all return no content); text comes only from nodeRepl.write(), nodeRepl.emitImage(), and the auto-included state of entry APIs (getState/getApp/getTab).

findings: pi 0.99.1 does not fire agent_before_settle for aborted runs; the last assistant message carries stopReason `error` with errorMessage `This operation was aborted` when the abort lands during tool execution. The bridge therefore marks the turn aborted when a bridged call is cancelled through the signal and when agent_end shows an abort.

node_repl serializes tools/call requests: turn_ended sent while a cancelled js is still running is answered only after that js completes. The 10 s timeout used first expired; 120 s and not awaiting the call fixed it.
The REPL returns no content for bare expression values; models must use nodeRepl.write()/emitImage(). Entry APIs (getState/getApp/getTab) auto-include their state.
The tool description's first-call rule is enforced by capable models: a prompt asking for arbitrary code as the first call is refused.
The log redaction regex (/key/i) hides fields such as `trustedServiceKeys`; the package's own log fields avoid the word key.
unresolved: Overlay (`ChatGPT is using your computer`) behavior after turn_ended was not observable while Codex Desktop runs its own session.
Whether to send js_reset after a cancelled js call so a long-running action stops immediately (Codex does not; left as is).
Built-in MCP coexistence with a configured mcp.json server was not exercised (none configured).
/reload path and Windows process-tree termination (StdioTransport uses taskkill /T on win32) are untested.
